sessions.title: After the AI Hype – What’s Real, and What’s Next
sessions.description: Artificial Intelligence dominates the headlines, driving unprecedented attention and expectations—but much of the conversation is fueled by hype. At the same time, real breakthroughs are transforming industries and reshaping how businesses and developers work. This session explores the current AI surge: what’s real, what’s exaggerated, and where organizations are achieving meaningful results today. It also examines the mechanics of a hype cycle, its inevitable decline, and what the aftermath will mean for the future of AI technologies.

sessions.title: Building a real-time collaborative editor
sessions.description:
Have you ever wondered what it takes to develop a solution similar to Google Docs and then build on top of it with extra layers of security and functionality?

During the planning phase of a military operation, there are multiple text documents that need to be updated simultaneously by multiple users. At the same time, there is a requirement to provide security in air-gapped deployments.

As such, a solution that follows high standards for security, performance and quality is required.

Within my presentation, I will be describing an embedded solution based on advanced operational transformation algorithms which allows real-time secure collaborative editing, as well as several challenges that we have faced during development and how we managed to overcome each of them.

sessions.title: Utvikler, utvikler, det er et norsk ord i koden din!
sessions.description:
Spør en gruppe utviklere om hva de synes om bruke norsk i kildekode. Du kommer til å få mange svar, de fleste av dem negative. Men hvorfor er det en stille aksept for at utvikling i Norge skal skje på engelsk, når de fleste norsktalende utviklere forstår og uttrykker seg bedre på norsk? Denne antagelsen, og mange andre språklige «sannheter» som vi utviklere omgir oss med, kommer denne virvelvinden av et foredrag til å røske tak i.

Dette foredraget er for alle som elsker språk, både språkene brukt av oss mennesker og de brukt av datamaskiner. I løpet av foredraget kommer vi til å gjøre landfall over temaer som hvordan naturlige språk og informatikk har påvirket hverandre, på hvilken måte språklige metaforer i programmering og kodeverktøy hjelper utviklere å tenke, bruk av norsk og andre morsmål i kildekode og hvordan programmering på norsk kunne sett ut. På slutten av foredraget, når stormen har lagt seg, så vil du se forholdet mellom språk og programmering på en ny måte.

sessions.title: The Way of the Monad. Writing Cleaner, Safer Code that is Easier to Test
sessions.description:
After decades of coding, functional logic fundamentally changed how I work. What started as porting Scala’s Try to Java became a decade of building robust systems in TypeScript and C#. By using monads, our code became easier to test and more predictable.

This hands-on talk skips Haskell theory for practical Java, C#, and TypeScript examples. Learn to eliminate nulls, skip try-catch blocks, and simplify logic.

You’ll learn:

* Monads Demystified: What they are and how to spot them.
* Practical Patterns: Using Try, Option, and Either to replace nested ifs.
* Clean Logic: Why starting methods with return leads to safer code.
* Cross-Platform: Applying these ideas to any stack with live examples.

Stop fighting boilerplate. Learn how functional design simplifies your flow and failure states.

sessions.title: State of AI UX in 2026
sessions.description:
As teams race to find ways to bring AI into their products, many discover that many AI features have very low retention, low usage and little to none trust in its accuracy and reliability. Many chatbots and assistants are painfully slow, repetitive, verbose and hard to make work — users have to meticulously explain to AI just what exactly they need — over and over and over again.

So what exactly do teams do to fix it? How do we design AI experiences that people understand, value and perhaps even fall in love with? How fast is AI actually moving these days? How do we measure the quality of an AI experience? And how do we build confidence and trust in its use? Well, let’s find out!

In this session with Vitaly Friedman, senior UX Lead with the European Parliament and also working with small and large clients around the world on embedding AI into their work, we’ll explore where users struggle and get annoyed, and when users succeed and become more effective. From quiet AI to AI-first, from voice UX to agentic experiences, from design patterns for building trust to technical constraints and limitations — and the look into what’s coming up next.

sessions.title: Lokalt lavt skydekke - Nasjonal kontroll, skyløsninger og trygge data
sessions.description:
Vi har på ingen måte lenger kontroll på hvem som er våre venner og fiender. De som i går var venner som vi stolte på kan nå gi vekk våre mest betrodde hemmeligheter. Kontroll på hvem som kan lese data og hvor disse sendes blir stadig mer betent, ikke bare for nasjonalstater, men også for bedrifter og organisasjoner. 

Den stadig mer fragmenterte situasjonen der ulike skyløsninger er sammenvevd på komplett uforståelige måter er i ferd med å bli normalen. I selskaper som driver med IT-drift er det blitt et fast sosialt innslag å snakke om sist en eller flere av de større  amerikanske (offentlige) skyleverandørene rev ned et sted mellom 20 og 70 % av all Internett-trafikk gjennom en konfigurasjons-feil.
Foredraget utforsker ulike måter å bygge (høytilgjengelige|nasjonale|lokale) tjenester uten å havne i "avhengighetsfella" hos de store og sørge for at man har tjenester som lett lar seg kjøre flere steder. 
Vi ser på behov for nasjonal kontroll, byggesteiner for lokale skyløsninger, regionale skyløsninger og metoder for å drifte tjenester mer selvstendig med velprøvde verktøy.

Dersom det er tid blir det nok et sveip innom godbiter som "Det er 0 dager siden det var DNS", "We made an error to our configuration that impacted SOME (..all) of our users", "Select (all) customers are seeing prolonged deployment time frames (we can't serve anyone and we don't know when we're back online)" og den gode gamle "503 - the server made an error".

_KAN_ kjøres på 20 min, men bør ha 40..

sessions.title: Level Up Accessibility Testing with Playwright
sessions.description:
Accessibility is a core part of building inclusive, user-friendly products. However, many teams still struggle to test accessibility effectively. What if it were as easy and automated as your end-to-end tests?

In this talk, we'll explore why accessibility matters, how it impacts real users, and what the WCAG guidelines mean for developers. From there, you'll get a quick introduction to Playwright, Microsoft's end-to-end testing framework, and see how it can go beyond functional testing to catch accessibility issues early.

sessions.title: Utbrenthet fra toppen – en historie om å falle, lære og reise seg igjen
sessions.description:
Lederskap blir ofte sett på som en rolle preget av styrke og motstandskraft, men hva skjer når presset blir for stort?
I dette foredraget deler jeg min personlige historie om å møte veggen som leder, øyeblikket da jeg innså at jeg ikke lenger kunne fortsette, og den lange veien tilbake til balanse og velvære.

Gjennom denne reisen har jeg lært å gjenkjenne viktige faresignaler for utbrenthet, og jeg ønsker å dele praktiske råd til ledere og konsulenter om hvordan de kan beskytte seg før det er for sent.
Målet mitt er å gi en ærlig refleksjon som andre kan kjenne seg igjen i, kombinert med konkrete tiltak for å forebygge utbrenthet og bevare motstandskraft i krevende roller.

Hovedpunkter:

- Hvordan oppdage tidlige varselsignaler på utbrenthet.
- Praktiske steg for å komme seg og bygge varig motstandskraft.
- Råd for å bevare balansen.

sessions.title: Embedded Rust in Production
sessions.description:
Often when new languages like Rust get introduced, it starts with a hobby project and simple proof of concepts. But what does it take to go beyond that and use it in production?

Akiles is a manufacturer of access control devices and have been using Rust to program our embedded devices for over 4 years. Embedded Rust projects like Embassy started at Akiles, and have since flourished and grown into a widely used open source project.

This talk will give an introduction to the Embedded Rust ecosystem, async Rust, and share our experience using Rust in production at Akiles.

sessions.title: Let's break some WCAG rules
sessions.description:
Let's experience a web that's not made for you!

This talk is not a checklist of rules. It’s an interactive wake-up call.
15–25% of the population needs websites to accommodate different types of disabilities. Still, 94.8% of websites contain accessibility issues that make them harder to use.

It’s not because we don’t want to develop accessible websites and applications.
But we often lack knowledge and perspective. We build based on our own experience because that’s what we know. In this talk, you’ll get to experience how our applications work for someone with a screen reader, low vision, or limited motor control, and feel firsthand the challenges they face.

The talk combines knowledge, practice, and lived experience to raise your awareness of accessibility on the web and how small changes can make a huge difference.

You'll see the most common mistakes in action, who they affect, and how to fix them. So come experience the world through someone else's senses, and learn how to be a more accessible developer.

sessions.title: Ikke alle angrep er slemme: DDoS innenfra og utenfra
sessions.description: Det siste året har interessen for NRK.no økt blant utenlandske stormakter. Selv om det er hyggelig å være populær kan det noen ganger bli litt for mye. I denne presentasjonen skal vi gå gjennom hvordan DDoS-angrep oppleves hos NRK.no og hvordan vi prøver å minske konsekvensene når angrepene skjer. Vi skal også se at ikke alle angrep er fiendtlige eller kommer utenifra.

sessions.title: Åtte måter å feile med innsikt, og ni måter å lykkes
sessions.description:
Et produkts brukeropplevelse er summen av tusen store og små beslutninger. Svært mange av disse beslutningene tas på usikkert grunnlag, og resultatene blir deretter. 

Innsiktsentusiast Isak Falch er opptatt av at vi må synliggjøre usikkerhet og risiko for å skape læringstørst i virksomhetene vi jobber med. I dette foredraget ser han på hvordan vi kan bruke designverktøy til å evaluere vår egen innsiktspraksis, og hva som skal til for å bli en lærende organisasjon.

sessions.title: Sporer alle skip i norske farvann - Hvordan vi bygger dataplattform for Kystverket
sessions.description:
Norge er en nasjon bygget av fiskere, sjømenn og en lang historie på havet. Nå bygger Kystverket en dataplattform som skal bidra til at Norge blir verdens mest effektive kystnasjon. 

Hver dag strømmer over 100 millioner rader med AIS-data fra fartøy gjennom plattformen uten problemer. Hør hvordan vi bruker disse dataene til å vurdere om skip er på kollisjonskurs, forbedre effektiviteten for å spare klimautslipp, og hvordan vi knytter dette sammen med mange andre datakilder, ved hjelp av Azure og Databricks. 

I dette foredraget tar Peter oss gjennom bakgrunnen for dataplattformen, hvordan teamet ble bygget opp for å levere effektivt, og hvordan Kystverket levere data og analyser for å løse samfunnsoppdraget sitt.

sessions.title: Architecture is a Conversation, Not a Diagram
sessions.description:
Five things our industry treats as truth about software architecture. None of them hold up. UML was a vendor interop play from 1994, not a communication tool. Architecture is not an artifact. It is an understanding that lives in conversation. Natural language is the only notation everyone in the room already compiles.

I spent twenty-five years doing architecture. I was a student volunteer at OOPSLA 1998. I published a design pattern at EuroPLoP 1999. I believed the box-and-arrow gospel for two decades.

Then I went back and read what Christopher Alexander, Peter Naur, Alan Kay, Martin Fowler, and Rich Hickey actually wrote. What I found was uncomfortable: we kept the notation and abandoned the meaning.

This talk takes five beliefs most teams treat as architectural truth and pulls them apart. That architecture requires formal notation. That it is a visual discipline. That the architect's job is to produce artifacts. That decisions should be made upfront. That documentation solves the knowledge problem.

I show what the giants actually said, what I built to test the idea (a small experiment called ConvArch), and what it taught me about feedback loops in architecture. I will also be honest about the limits of my own argument. Conversation without verification is just a nicer way to be wrong together. Five people confidently agreeing in a room is still a confident guess.

sessions.title: Almost hired: the silent filters of belonging
sessions.description:
What truly shapes us without us even noticing? Sometimes, it’s not the hard stops that define our path, it’s the silent redirections, the invisible “no’s,” and the things no one says out loud. 
This talk reveals the quiet, systemic ways highly skilled immigrants are shaped - not just by the cultures they enter, but by the coded preferences that decide who gets to belong.

I moved to Norway for a job, but soon my employer went bankrupt just months after I arrived. And so began nine months of searching. Nine months of being “almost chosen.” I reached final interviews again and again. Each time, I was told I was an excellent candidate. But each time, the job went to a Norwegian.
Not because they were better. But because they were familiar.

This isn’t a conspiracy - it’s a pattern. A silent comfort with the known. A national culture that values sameness, even when it claims to welcome diversity. And it has a cost: not just to people like me, but to innovation, creativity, and the richness of perspective that companies quietly forfeit.

This talk invites audiences to consider the invisible forces: comfort and unconscious bias that shape careers and cultures more than we care to admit. And it offers a vision of what we could gain if we finally let go of our fear of difference.
Because real inclusion doesn’t happen when we let people in. It happens when we let them stay whole.

sessions.title: AI is not your UX researcher
sessions.description:
Fifteen years ago, I studied AI. I built neural networks, worked with robots, and was excited by the idea of making systems smarter. But I eventually found myself asking a different question: why make things smarter if we are not making them better? That question led me into UX research.

Today, AI is at the centre of product development. It helps us write, analyse, ideate, summarise, and move faster. But it is also starting to play a more questionable role: teams are asking AI to validate product ideas, simulate user feedback, create personas, and tell them what users need.

This talk is about how to use AI well in UX research and where to draw the line.

AI can make UX research faster, clearer, and easier to share. Used well, it can support the work around research and help teams think more sharply. But it cannot replace what matters most: contact with real users. It cannot observe real behaviour, understand context, or reveal the messy reality of how people actually use products.

AI can make your ideas sound convincing. UX research tells you whether they are true.

sessions.title: View Transitions: The brand-new browser API that will blow your mind
sessions.description:
Have you ever wondered why a well-made native app often feels way smoother than a similar web page? The answer is that native apps have long wielded the full power of seamless transitions, while on the web we have had to use heavy JavaScript frameworks to accomplish anything remotely similar.

That ends now! In this talk we will take a look at the brand new View Transitions API, a browser API that lets you control every aspect of the transition between web pages with just a few lines of CSS. In addition to seeing what the API is capable of we will dive under the hood to see how exactly the API does its magic.

sessions.title: Kunnskap har et byggesteg: Praktisk context-engineering for agenter
sessions.description:
Å holde kontroll på kontekstvinduet til AI-kodeagenter kan være overraskende krevende. De gjetter i stedet for å lese dokumentasjonen, og produserer dårlig kode. Du tvinger de til å lese mer, og så mister de tråden i oppgaven de egentlig skulle løse. Eller de bruker tusenvis av tokens på dokumentasjon, skills og irrelevante filer, bare for å gjøre en liten endring i en template-fil. 

Vi bygde et telemetridrevet kunnskapssystem for å styre konteksten agentene faktisk får tilgang til. Ved å analysere våre kodesesjoner i et stort monorepo kunne vi se hvor de gikk seg vill, hva de burde lest først, og hvor dokumentasjonen, strukturen eller arbeidsflyten sviktet. Resultatet er et system som selv kan foreslå hvor det er mangler, og som forbedrer seg selv over tid. 

I dette foredraget viser jeg hvordan du kan unngå “agent compliance theatre”, sette opp praktiske hooks og telemetri, og gjøre context-engineering til en datadrevet øvelse i stedet for magefølelse. Du går ut med konkrete mønstre du kan bruke fra dag én. Enten du sitter på 20 000 linjer kode eller over én million.

sessions.title: Trøbbel i Trøndelag: AtB-appen låser seg!
sessions.description:
Hva gjør du når en feil slår inn for bare 0.02% av brukerne? Det er jo ikke et stort tall, skal du bry deg?

Jo, det bør du! Det skjer nemlig noe interessant når du har mange nok brukere. Tekniske stordriftsulemper slår inn. 
Feil som er vanskelig å reprodusere, og skjer prosentvis ganske sjeldent, vil oppstå hele tiden med mange nok brukere.

En slik subtil feil klarte jeg å introdusere i AtB-appen når jeg oppgraderte React Native-rammeverket. Dette gjorde at appen frøs fullstendig for hundrevis av brukere hver dag når de skulle vise billetten sin.   

I dette foredraget kommer jeg til å fortelle hvordan vi gikk fram for å fikse feilen. Vi kommer innom native kræsj-logger med race conditions i Bugsnag, profilering av ytelse i DevTools, og ulike forsøk på å fikse dette med Skia, React Compiler og native-kode.

Det du kommer til å sitte igjen med er hvordan en skal feilsøke i grenselandet mellom JavaScript og native-kode. Og hvilke typiske fallgruver en bør unngå når en skal videreutvikle modne React- og React Native-apper.

sessions.title: Did you remember to think? A critical eye on AI
sessions.description: Are you among those that are tired of the hustle and bustle to "use AI at any cost", and that questions the fact that AI is presented like the solution, not the tool? Are you sick of getting stressed about becoming outdated and set aside because you don't want to use AI for everything? A little tired of the hype and want to hear someone talk about the downsides too? Then this is the talk for you!

sessions.title: Passkeys: Enklere enn du tror. Slik implementerer du støtte for det
sessions.description:
Passord er en av de største svakhetene i moderne sikkerhet – de er vanskelige å huske, enkle å kompromittere, og frustrerende å bruke. Passkeys representerer et fundamentalt skifte i hvordan vi tenker på autentisering.

I dette foredraget får du en praktisk og teknisk innføring i hvordan passkeys fungerer, hva som skjer “under panseret”, og hvorfor de er både sikrere og enklere enn tradisjonelle passord. Vi går gjennom hvordan WebAuthn og FIDO2 muliggjør passordløs pålogging, og hvordan dette faktisk fungerer i nettleseren og på tvers av enheter.

Du får også se en live demonstrasjon av hvordan man implementerer passkeys i en moderne webapplikasjon – fra registrering til innlogging – med fokus på hvor overraskende lite som skal til for å komme i gang.

Til slutt ser vi på hvordan utviklere kan bidra til å senke terskelen for trygg autentisering for brukerne sine og hvordan passordmanagere spiller en nøkkelrolle i å gjøre passkeys praktiske i hverdagen.

Målet med foredraget er at du skal sitte igjen med både forståelsen og selvtilliten til å implementere støtte for passkeys selv.

sessions.title: Code reviews for mennesker
sessions.description:
I teknologiteam er vi gode på feedback; i alle fall på kode.

Vi gjør code reviews, diskuterer arkitektur og analyserer feil i produksjon. Men når det gjelder hvordan vi samarbeider, hvordan vi opptrer i møter, hvordan vi påvirker hverandre og hvordan vi kan bli bedre som team. Da blir det ofte stille.

Ikke fordi vi ikke bryr oss, men fordi vi mangler språk og struktur.

I denne sesjonen viser jeg hvordan utviklingsteam kan gjøre tilbakemeldinger mer konkrete, trygge og nyttige i hverdagen. Med enkle modeller som SBI, IDEA og CEDAR kan feedback bli mindre awkward og mer verdifull både for enkeltpersoner, for teamet og for prosjektet.

Jeg vil gi:

* enkel modell for å gi konkrete tilbakemeldinger
* verktøy for å skape endring uten å skape motstand
* eksempler fra teknologiteam og prosjektarbeid

Målet er ikke mer teori, men noe du kan bruke i neste samtale med en kollega.

For akkurat som kode blir bedre gjennom review, blir team bedre gjennom tilbakemeldinger.

sessions.title: React Won. So Why Does Everything Feel Broken?
sessions.description:
React launched with a clear goal: to proudly only be the V in MVC. In the world of frameworks, where Angular and Ember ruled, React planted its flag as a UI library with no opinions about routing or state. 

Over 10 years later, we now see they skipped the entire framework step and went on to become a platform. Server Components, the compiler, multiple output modes. These platform decisions reshaping our mental models on how we think about building for the web.

While React was busy becoming infrastructure, the actual web platform kept evolving. The browser is more capable than ever, yet most developers never reach for any of it. React casts such a long shadow that the real platform underneath has become invisible.

AI is making this worse. AI, as the self-referential technology it is, has been trained to enforce past winners rather than future ones. Ask an AI to build a UI and it will reach for React by default, regardless of whether React is the right tool.

React won by pushing the web forward, but now it holds us back.

It is time for whatever comes next. I have been building with React for well over ten years. In 2014 a stranger thanked me for helping bring pure function components into React, and I have spent the years since writing, speaking, doing podcast, and building open source tooling around it. Nobody is more surprised than me that I am making this argument, but here we are.

sessions.title: Challenges with OpenTelemetry tracing on the client
sessions.description: Vi i DIPS AS har tatt i bruk distribuert sporing fra klientapplikasjoner for å gjøre det enklere å feilsøke og forstå den faktiske brukeropplevde ytelsen i en klassisk enterprise‑applikasjon. Å bruke OpenTelemetry for distribuert sporing på klientsiden byr imidlertid på en rekke utfordringer. I denne presentasjonen deler vi erfaringene våre og viser noen av de mest interessante problemstillingene vi har støtt på underveis.

sessions.title: Designer, slutt å være så snill!
sessions.description:
Som designere og fagpersoner må vi tørre å gjøre det som er ukomfortabelt. Vi må ta de samtalene vi helst vil unngå, utfordre beslutninger vi er uenige i, og stå i rom der vi føler oss uvelkomne, dersom det er det som skal til for å skape verdi. Verdi for organisasjonen og for brukeren. 
Designere sitter på en unik forståelse av brukere, prosesser og organisasjon. Men den innsikten blir verdiløs hvis vi bare bruker den i trygge omgivelser. Å levere skisser og prototyper er komfortabelt. Å sette seg ved bordet der strategien formes, og si ifra når den mangler virkelighetskontakt, det kan være ukomfortabelt. Men noen ganger er det nettopp det jobben krever.
Dette foredraget handler om hva det betyr å gå ut av komfortsonen: å prioritere det som er nødvendig fremfor det som er behagelig, å ta ansvar utover eget fagfelt, og å tåle friksjon for å skape reell endring. Frustrert over dårlige beslutninger ovenfra? Da holder det ikke å sitte stille og designe videre. Tre ut av den trygge boblen og påvirk.

sessions.title: Did My Deploy Degrade Production? Detecting Bad Deploys with Math
sessions.description:
When you deploy some code, do you know its impact on your production stats, like memory usage, request duration, error rates? If you wanted to know if your code improved or deteriorated the speed of SQL queries, would you know where to get this data?

We collect a lot of metrics in production systems, but we usually set alerts only when these metrics cross a hardcoded threshold, which is often somewhat randomly chosen. But most metrics don't go "unhealthy" overnight, they are usually slowly pushed towards the threshold for a while before they reach the threshold.

Wouldn't it be great if we could detect these changes soon after a code change is out rather than 2 months later.

Welcome to the wonderful world of automated health detection, where we teach Python to answer the eternal question: "Does my code have undesired side effects?".

I'm not a data scientist. But a few years ago, I built a Python system that answers this question automatically. It does so by using collecting data points every 2 minutes, analyzing 14 days of past metric data and alerting us when the data trajectory changes.

I’ll walk through how the algorithm works, how it was built and some of it's tricks.

The system has been running in production for years and is actively used to detect regressions and behavioral changes in real-world systems.

Based on: https://www.ines-panker.com/2026/02/18/impact-of-a-deploy.html

sessions.title: Designet ditt er ikke ferdig før det faktisk kjører
sessions.description:
Hvordan kan vi sørge for at design ikke bare forblir en fin skisse på papiret, men faktisk skaper fremdrift? Som designere jobber vi allerede systematisk, med komponenter, strukturer og informasjonsmodeller. Likevel har jeg opplevd mange ganger at deler av denne systemtenkningen går tapt når designet overleveres til utvikling, til tross for hvor tett på man prøver å være. Designet må tolkes og bygges opp på nytt.

I denne praten ønsker jeg å dele erfaringer fra å bruke frontend-kode som en del av skisseprosessen, støttet av AI-verktøy i Visual Studio Code. Ikke for å gjøre designere til utviklere, men for å vise et nytt verktøy man kan bruke for å kommunisere intensjonen bak designet (ikke bare UI, men systemet) til utviklere. Og ikke minst hvordan man selv kan få testet idéer mye mer skalerbart og i et dynamisk miljø.

Med talken min så ønsker jeg å:
- vise hvordan skissering i kode kan gi et godt verktøy for å kommunisere design
- vise hvordan vi som designere kan med dette gi mer tydeligere forventning også til backend
- gjøre det mulig å raskt skissere og iterere ved hjelp av AI (og faktisk fremdeles ha kontroll over UI-et)
- bidra til at designets struktur og intensjon i større grad overlever overgangen til kode
- gir muligheter til å samarbeide på tvers på en ny måte

sessions.title: Down to Earth: Receiving Data from Orbiting Observatories
sessions.description:
An introduction to earth observation from satellites in polar orbit, the challenges that must be overcome in acquiring the data from the satellites, and how this is done at 
Space Ground Systems.
Includes a demonstration showing a live data acquisition.

sessions.title: Meditations on Code As Art
sessions.description:
Code can be beautiful, elegant and performant, but can it deliberately be artistic?

Despite how important and prolific software and programming have become over the last 50 years the general public still have a very loose understanding of what software actually is.

This hasn't been lost of the people that build the software, who often slowly try and capture themselves in the work that they do.

In this talk we'll take a look at some examples through history of seeing the humans behind the code they write as they imprint themselves on their work and we'll consider if it's possible to deliberately make art by manipulating the form and design of software itself.

A talk for everyone wanting to be seen in the work, or understand their own creative urge.

sessions.title: No More Big Bang: Make Your Releases Bulletproof
sessions.description:
Have you ever needed to stop a release of your microservice and had to wait until other parts of the system got released first? Have you ever needed to roll back to the previous version of your service because its API wasn’t compatible with the consumers? Have you ever experienced code freezes?

Chances are, you have experienced many of those, but there is good news: in most situations, you can avoid those issues and obtain truly independent deployments and releases. Many patterns and strategies can help you untangle your dependency on changes in other services (and vice versa) and make your team's life much easier and less stressful. You will hear about API versioning, API Evolution Patterns, Contract Testing, Database Migrations and more.

During this talk, you will learn the fundamentals of introducing changes in APIs and database in a way that is backward and forward compatible, how to prevent broken integrations with other services and frontend applications. I will show the proper mindset of a developer, automatic ways to prevent those issues, and tools that can help you with that.

I look forward to seeing you at my talk!

sessions.title: An Opinionated Guide to Bulletproof APIs (with code examples)
sessions.description:
Writing a "Hello World" endpoint is easy. But building an API that is secure, observable, and capable of evolving without breaking every client? That’s where the real engineering happens. We often pollute our business logic with validation, security checks, and boilerplate, creating a maintenance nightmare.

It’s time to clean up our act. In this session, we’ll move beyond basic CRUD to explore 5 essential patterns for building production-grade APIs. We will combine standard Jakarta EE/MicroProfile features with powerful custom implementations to tackle the cross-cutting concerns that matter most.

The examples will be in Java, but the knowledge can be applied to  the framework and language of your choosing.

sessions.title: Developers in the Dark Forest
sessions.description:
Developers used to have a home on the internet. Stack Overflow was our oracle. Twitter was our town square. Open source repos were our collective workshop. But something has gone wrong. Stack Overflow sits abandoned. Twitter lost its name and its soul. Open source repos are filled with AI-generated code that feels hollow. New "developer platforms" promise community but nobody shows up. The internet isn't just dying for everyone. It's dying for the people who built it.

So we've gone underground into DMs, Discord servers, private Slacks. We're hiding at the edges of a web that doesn't feel like ours anymore. Two theories explain what happened to us. The "dark forest theory" suggests the public internet became hostile: bad actors, bots, trolls, and scrapers turned every public space into a minefield. So we learned to stay quiet, share less, and keep our real conversations private. The "dead internet theory" goes further: most of the content we see online is now generated by bots, for bots. We're not just hiding from threats anymore. We're performing for an audience that might not even be human, contributing to repositories that AI will scrape, answering questions that ChatGPT will repackage. 

This talk explores how these forces changed the developer internet, what it means to build and learn when the web feels broken, and whether we can still find each other.

sessions.title: Tips til hvordan du gjør løsningen din litt grønnere
sessions.description:
Hver gang vi besøker et nettsted eller bruker en digital tjeneste, går det med energi – både på serverne som leverer dataene, og på enhetene som viser dem. Men hvorfor har nettsider og digitale produkter blitt så tunge? De siste 10 årene har vekten på en gjennomsnittlig nettside faktisk doblet seg. Allerede før KI-bølgen så utgjorde utslippet fra IT-sektoren mer enn flybransjen.

Omtrent 80 % av de digitale utslippene bestemmes allerede i designfasen, gjennom valg vi tar som utviklere og designere. Uten bevissthet rundt dette ender vi lett opp med unødvendig tunge og energikrevende løsninger.

I dette foredraget får du tips til hvordan du kan kutte ned på «vekten» i løsningen din, redusere energiforbruket og samtidig gjøre den raskere.

sessions.title: What’s New in Web? 2026 Edition
sessions.description: Christian is a member of the World Wide Web’s architecture board, the Technical Architecture Group (TAG) of W3C. As such, he has insights into what’s going on in the web platform. In his session, you'll gain insights into the latest discussions among standards bodies, browser vendors, and web developers. And you have the opportunity to report your wishes back to the Web’s architecture board. Don't miss this opportunity to stay updated on the forefront of web technologies.

sessions.title: Aspire 13: One AppHost, Many Languages
sessions.description:
Aspire is not just for .NET. With Aspire 13, you can bring Python, Node.js, Go, Java, and C# services into a single AppHost and manage them as one local development experience. In this session, we will build and explore a set of polyglot sample applications using Flask, Django, React, Go, Java, and .NET.

We will start with the pain Aspire helps remove: service discovery confusion, scattered configuration, fragile startup order, and READMEs full of manual steps. You will see how AddPythonApp, AddNpmApp, and AddDockerfile bring different runtimes into the Aspire lifecycle, and how service references and environment variables replace hardcoded URLs and duplicated .env files. We will also use Aspire’s dashboard to view traces, logs, and metrics from multiple languages in one place.

Along the way, we will cover the patterns teams need when a repo grows beyond one stack: dependency ordering, health checks, connection-string injection, and debugging requests across frontend and backend services. We will close by looking at the Aspire CLI workflow, repo structure, CI and deployment automation, and where Azure fits when you are ready to move beyond local development.

sessions.title: Jaktet av Pac-Man
sessions.description:
Smart-TV-er selges som passive bokser for å se Netflix, men de er datamaskiner du ikke har admin på, og de snakker med hundrevis av eksterne endepunkter du aldri har samtykket til. I denne sesjonen åpner jeg motorpanseret på en LG WebOS-TV og viser hvordan jeg, gjennom systematisk PCAP-analyse, identifiserte Bright Data SDK pakket inn i en tilsynelatende uskyldig kasualspill-app (Pac-Man by Playworks). Resultatet: TV-en min har deler av tiden vært en residential proxy-node i et kommersielt nettverk.

Jeg deler metodikken (capture-oppsett, isolering av TV-trafikk, sammenligning med en kontrollert EarnApp-endepunkt på en mobiltelefon), de konkrete funnene (domener, trafikkmønstre, IOC-er), og hvordan dette eksponerer en supply chain-risiko få SOC-er overvåker i dag. 

Vi vil også gå inn på hva det er Smart-TV produsentene og selskaper som Bright Data faktisk benytter denen kapasiteten til og hva de typisk høster av data om deg og dine seervaner

sessions.title: How We Test an AI Chatbot in the Biggest Pharmacy Chain of Norway
sessions.description:
In early 2024, I developed an AI-powered RAG-based chatbot for Apotek 1, the largest pharmacy chain in Norway. This assistant helps pharmacists find accurate internal information across more than 450 locations.

While developing the chatbot was a great achievement, testing it turned out to be a challenge. Every time we changed a single prompt, model parameter, or retrieval setting, we had to verify the impact. Waiting for deployments or relying on third-party tools wasn’t good enough.

I needed something fast, simple, and tailored to our needs, so I built it myself :)

In this talk, I’ll share how I designed and implemented our custom chatbot testing tool in just a few days. You’ll see how such tools can give you full control, speed up iteration, and avoid regressions. The session includes code examples, practical tips, and lessons learned.

By the end, you'll understand how to implement your own lightweight testing setup, without relying on expensive or complex tools.

I look forward to seeing you at my talk!

sessions.title: Gammal font, nye kurver
sessions.description:
Digitalisering av gamle fontar har både kulturell og historisk verdi, men det skal mange utfordringar til før det fungerer optimalt på skjerm. Nye bokstavar og diakritiske teikn må til for å dekke det latinske skriftspråket, samtidig som identiteten skal bevares. 

Bli med inn i ein prosess fylt av Bézier-kurver, kinkar og kerning, og få eit innblikk i korleis små justeringar og optiske vurderingar kan gi store forbedringar for lesbarheit og digital bruk. 

Denne presentasjonen passar for deg som er nysgjerrig på skriftddesign og produksjon av fontar, og som har lyst til å lære meir om korleis ein font blir til.

sessions.title: Your Testing Strategy is broken - lets fix it!
sessions.description: Testing is essential for delivering reliable software, but too often, teams fall into the trap of testing everything and testing it poorly. Endless unit tests for trivial code create a false sense of security while ignoring the areas that matter most—like how your system behaves when it really counts. This session takes a hard look at what makes a good testing strategy. Instead of chasing meaningless metrics like 100% coverage, learn how to test behaviors, focus on integration points, and embrace a leaner, smarter approach to quality assurance. Your users don’t care about how many tests you’ve written—they care about software that works. This is your guide to writing fewer tests, but better ones, that actually make a difference.

sessions.title: Java Sucks (So C# Didn't Have To)
sessions.description:
Using Java as an everyday language can be absolutely infuriating. It's verbose and clunky, with all roads seemingly pointing to null. These are faults that users of other languages (especially of C#) love to point out.

At the same time, Java is mature, stable, backwards compatible, and runs just about anywhere. The community is pretty cool too!

This talk takes a light-hearted, warts-and-all look at some of the more frustrating aspects of Java, how the language has evolved over time and where it's headed next. A discussion on the consequences of language design decisions that can be enjoyed by programmers of all languages, but especially by C# users.

Expect to laugh, and yes maybe even cry, as we try to make sense of the beast that puts food on the table for millions of developers worldwide

We will cover:
- Pivotal early design decisions such as checked exceptions and generics and how we still pay for those decisions today (that is, why do lambdas suck so bad?)
- How Java has influenced the development of other programming languages, and vice versa
- Most controversial language design decisions of late and the associated fallouts

Java developers will leave this session feeling validated and with a renewed love for the language that keeps a large chunk of the world running. C# developers will leave this session with a renewed level of smugness.

sessions.title: The OG Social Network
sessions.description:
Long before Facebook, a social computing network known as Bulletin Board Systems (BBSes) emerged from improvised technology and grassroots labor. Built on homebrew computers, gadgets and phone lines, these systems became refuges for hackers and outcasts.

This talk tells the story of how computer hobbyists built a world-spanning social network during the 1970s and 80s, the technological innovations that made it possible, and the people who made it happen.

This is the story what impact volunteers operating outside institutional power can have when creating safe online spaces for cultural and political, and above all social interaction.

Maybe this social network wasn't a precursor to the internet, but a blueprint for what networked life can be when shaped primarily by its participants.

sessions.title: Hvem er Nicolai Winther?
sessions.description:
Hvem er Nicolai Winther? Og hvorfor later OpenAIs Whisper som om den er ham?
Det hele startet med en snedig detalj i en bloggpost: et navn som dukket opp på slutten av automatiske transkripsjoner – igjen og igjen. I norske podcaster, i avisartikler, i tekstfiler fra et offentlig mediatek i Madrid, til og med i en akademisk artikkel om transkribering av politiavhør.
Hvem er denne mannen, og hvorfor har en av verdens største AI-modeller bestemt seg for å kreditere ham for arbeid han aldri har gjort?
Lars tar deg med på en detektivjakt gjennom Whisper, hallusinasjoner og treningsdata – fra et tilfeldig Google-søk til en uventet samtale med personen bak navnet.
For deg som bygger tjenester på toppen av språkmodeller, jobber med transkribering, eller bare er nysgjerrig på hva som faktisk skjer inne i de svarte boksene vi stoler blindt på.
Du kommer til å google ham etterpå.

sessions.title: Engineering for Chaos: Software Architecture for Emergency Response
sessions.description:
Emergency medicine is chaos by default: connectivity disappears, devices fail, crews change mid-mission, and data must follow the patient — not the hardware.

This talk tells the real-world story of designing and building software used across ambulances, helicopters, and maritime units, running on Windows, iPad, Android, and the web, with full offline support and reliable synchronization.

Driven by harsh constraints, the architecture evolved toward an event-first approach where every change became an atomic unit for storage, transfer, and replay. You’ll hear how this enabled offline-first sync, multi-device collaboration, live handovers between teams, and consistent behavior across platforms.

This is not a theory talk. It’s a candid, experience-based story about architectural tradeoffs, unexpected challenges, and what actually worked when the software left localhost and entered real emergency environments.

sessions.title: Ubuntu as AI Compass for Healthy Human-AI Relationships
sessions.description: This keynote will address the issue of what is required of us as humanity to become relational cross-culturally, and therefore become better at relating with machines that flatten all our cultures into a predicted algorithm. The Ubuntu philosophy is the oldest known concept that defines what it means to be human and is captured in the saying, "I am because of who We are." In a time of global crises that touch every life on the planet, we are facing an unprecedented technological advancement happening faster than we can learn, reflect and relate. Ubuntu is the wisdom of relational intelligence. It breaks things down to a set of protocols for relating with chaos, uncertainty and new ways of being human together. Ubuntu philosophy is being applied to technoly at the design stage as a more ethical approach to creating solutions that solve real problems, while helping us maintain human dignity and a sense of belonging to one another. It is, as Desmond Tutu once declared, "Africa's gift to the world." This new version of Ubuntu cuts across cultures and geographies and attempts to bring peace and understanding in the technology space where there is a clash of values and ethics.

sessions.title: Kortslutning Live
sessions.description:

Kortslutning har siden 2018 tatt opp temaer vi møter på som utviklere i det daglige, alt fra menneskelige utfordringer til tekniske.

Vi gjentar gleden med kveldsunderholdning fra TDC2025 med nye dilemmaer, nye spørsmål og nye kortslutninger.

Sander Hoogendoorn is an independent dad, avid traveler, and lifelong software developer. With over 40 years of hands-on coding experience under his belt, he still ships code every day — because once a developer, always a developer.

Currently the CTO at iBOOD, Sander has led technology at companies such as ANVA, Quby, and Klaverblad, and was once Capgemini’s global agile thought leader. But don’t expect corporate buzzwords — Sander’s known for cutting through the fluff with a post-agile mindset and a healthy disregard for outdated best practices.

He helps teams and organizations break rules that need breaking — replacing heavyweight processes with lightweight thinking, and agile dogma with actual flow. If something’s slowing your team down, chances are he’s already ranted about it in a keynote.

Onstage, Sander brings code, stories, and sharp insights — whether he’s talking disruption, continuous delivery, microservices, monads (yes, really), software architecture, or the lost art of elegant code. His talks are fast-paced, thought-provoking, and never just theory.

Sander believes in small steps, critical thinking, and building stuff that works. No silver bullets. Just better software, made by better teams.
speakers.tagLine: Tools do not solve problems. Thinking does.

Vitaly loves beautiful content and does not give up easily. Born in Minsk, Belarus, he studied computer science and mathematics in Germany. While writing algebra proofs and preparing for software engineering at nights in the kitchen, at the same time he discovered passion for typography, interface design and writing. After working as a freelance designer and developer for 6 years, he co-founded Smashing Magazine back in 2006, a leading online magazine for designers and developers. His curiosity drove him from interface design to front-end to performance optimization to accessibility and back to user experience over all the years.

Vitaly is the author, co-author and editor of Smashing Books (https://www.smashingmagazine.com/books), and a curator of  Smashing Conferences (https://www.smashingconf.com). He is the UX lead with the European Parliament and Smashing Magazine (www.smashingmagazine.com) and front-end/UX consultant in Europe and abroad, working with large and small companies and organizations like Haufe-Lexware, Axel-Springer and others.

He also runs Measure UX (https://measure-ux.com) and Smart Interface Design Patterns (https://smart-interface-design-patterns.com), friendly video courses on UX and design patterns, along with a live UX training for passionate UX and product designers.

speakers.bio: Wakanyi Macharia-Hoffman is an African indigenous scholar born and raised in a forest in Kenya. She is an internationally recognised speaker working at the intersection of Ubuntu ethics to promote African relational intelligence in AI systems. She is the  Director for Responsible AI at the Inclusive AI Lab at Utrecht University, where she interprets Ubuntu wisdom for AI designers. She founded the African Folktales Project, a digital knowledge commons that treats folktales as living archives of Indigenous relational ethics, ecological intelligence, and social knowledge, now serving over 24,000 teachers across the African continent on the Ubuntu Education Hub online platform. Her children’s books—including Sala, Mountain Warrior—extend this work through literature that dignifies African ancestral intelligence and heritage. As a senior fellow at The New Institute, she contributed to research on new conceptions of human flourishing, aimed at reformulating the Sustainable Development Goals. She sits on the advisory board of the IDG Foundation and the Global Citizens Assembly. She is a global nomad and mother of four who has lived in nine countries on four continents. She, her husband and children are currently spread out in the Netherlands, Japan and the US.
speakers.tagLine: Ubuntu Ethics Interpreter/ Director of Sustainable AI Ethics
